# std/https.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/https.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

HTTPS (or any protocol over TLS 1.3) for programs on the
hosted target: core/tls13client over the sockets of std/net.bastio. The
server is authenticated against the roots the caller trusts (DER
certificates one after the other, as `host_read` gives a file of them),
and the random bytes and the time come from the system (`net_random`,
`net_now`). Two suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and
TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, with X25519), servers by IPv4 address or, with
`https_get_by_name`, by a name looked up through std/dns, no client
certificates and no resumption; see core/tls13client.bastio for what is checked and what is not.

`import "std/https.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md), [core/hkdf.bastio](core-hkdf.md), [core/tls13.bastio](core-tls13.md), [core/tls13hs.bastio](core-tls13hs.md), [core/aes.bastio](core-aes.md), [core/aesgcm.bastio](core-aesgcm.md), [core/chacha20.bastio](core-chacha20.md), [core/poly1305.bastio](core-poly1305.md), [core/chacha20poly1305.bastio](core-chacha20poly1305.md), [core/tls13record.bastio](core-tls13record.md), [core/x25519.bastio](core-x25519.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/ed25519.bastio](core-ed25519.md), [core/p256.bastio](core-p256.md), [core/p384.bastio](core-p384.md), [core/rsa.bastio](core-rsa.md), [core/x509.bastio](core-x509.md), [core/tls13client.bastio](core-tls13client.md), [core/num.bastio](core-num.md), [core/httpsurl.bastio](core-httpsurl.md), [core/dns.bastio](core-dns.md), [std/net.bastio](std-net.md), [std/host.bastio](std-host.md), [std/dns.bastio](std-dns.md), `examples/http/http.bastio`, [std/http.bastio](std-http.md).

## Types and constants

### `HttpsResult`

```bastio
struct HttpsResult { state: u64, error: u64, data: Bytes }
```

What a TLS exchange ended with: the `state` of the client (6 is a clean
close by the server, 7 a failure), its error code (see `tls13c_feed`; 0
when the connection broke without one) and the application data received.

### `HttpsReply`

```bastio
struct HttpsReply { status: u64, body: Bytes }
```

What `https_fetch` found: the status code of the last response and its body.

### `HttpsChunks`

```bastio
struct HttpsChunks { body: Bytes, end: u64 }
```

Internal: a chunked body decoded from data that already holds it: the
body, and the offset just behind the last chunk and its trailers.

## Functions

### `https_run`

```bastio
fn https_run(h: &Host, sock: u64, name: &Bytes, request: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, now: u64, random: &Bytes, session: &Bytes, key: &Bytes) -> HttpsResult
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(request) < 1073741824 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(session) == 32 && blen(key) == 32
```

Runs a TLS 1.3 exchange on the connected socket `sock`: the handshake with
the server `name` (checked against the certificate), then `request` as
application data, then everything the server sends until it closes.
`random`, `session` and `key` are 32 bytes each that nobody can predict
(use each once), `now` the time in seconds since 1970. The socket stays
open.

Example:

```bastio
// The server hangs up at once: the handshake never gets going.
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let name = bfrom("localhost");
let request = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
let roots = balloc(0);
let random = balloc(32);
let session = balloc(32);
let key = balloc(32);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    match net_connect(host, lo, net_port(host, s)) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            net_close(host, a);
            let r = https_run(host, c, name, request, roots, 1800000000, random, session, key);
            if r.state == 0 && r.error == 0 && blen(r.data) == 0 { bad = 0; }
            https_result_free(r);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(key);
bfree(session);
bfree(random);
bfree(roots);
bfree(request);
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `https_result_free`

```bastio
fn https_result_free(r: HttpsResult)
```

Frees a result (see `https_run`).

### `https_request`

```bastio
fn https_request(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64, name: &Bytes, request: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(request) < 1073741824 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

Connects to `ip`:`port`, runs a TLS exchange with the server `name` (see
`https_run`) and returns what the server sent after `request`, if it ended
with a close_notify (a connection that is cut off, which could hide a
truncated answer, gives `None`, as does any failure of the handshake).

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1.
let name = bfrom("localhost");
let request = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
let roots = balloc(0);
let mut bad = 0;
match https_request(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1, name, request, roots) {
  Option::Some(r) => { bfree(r); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(roots);
bfree(request);
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `https_exchange`

```bastio
fn https_exchange(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64, name: &Bytes, request: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes) -> Option[HttpsResult]
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(request) < 1073741824 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

Like `https_request`, but gives the whole result whatever state the
exchange ended in (6 for a close_notify, 5 for a connection that was cut
off after the handshake, 7 for a failure), for a caller that can tell by
other means (a `Content-Length`) whether the answer is complete. `None`
only if there are no random bytes or the connection cannot be made.

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("localhost");
let request = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
let roots = balloc(0);
let mut bad = 0;
match https_exchange(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1, name, request, roots) {
  Option::Some(r) => { https_result_free(r); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(roots);
bfree(request);
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `https_exchange6`

```bastio
fn https_exchange6(h: &Host, ip6: &Bytes, port: u64, name: &Bytes, request: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes) -> Option[HttpsResult]
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(request) < 1073741824 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

`https_exchange` to the IPv6 address `ip6` (16 bytes, network order).

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("localhost");
let request = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
let roots = balloc(0);
let lo = bfrom("0123456789abcdef");
let mut bad = 0;
match https_exchange6(host, lo, 1, name, request, roots) {
  Option::Some(r) => { https_result_free(r); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(lo);
bfree(roots);
bfree(request);
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `https_get`

```bastio
fn https_get(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64, name: &Bytes, path: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(path) < 65536 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

A `GET` of `path` on the server `name` over HTTPS (HTTP/1.0 with the
connection closed after the answer): the whole answer, head and body.

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("localhost");
let path = bfrom("/");
let roots = balloc(0);
let mut bad = 0;
match https_get(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1, name, path, roots) {
  Option::Some(r) => { bfree(r); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(roots);
bfree(path);
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `https_get_by_name`

```bastio
fn https_get_by_name(h: &Host, name: &Bytes, port: u64, path: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(path) < 65536 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

`https_get` for a server given by `name`, whose address comes from the
system's resolver (std/dns; a name that is a dotted-quad address is used as
it is). `None` if the name does not resolve or the exchange fails.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1 of the loopback.
let name = bfrom("127.0.0.1");
let path = bfrom("/");
let roots = balloc(0);
let mut bad = 0;
match https_get_by_name(host, name, 1, path, roots) {
  Option::Some(r) => { bfree(r); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(roots);
bfree(path);
bfree(name);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `https_reply_free`

```bastio
fn https_reply_free(r: HttpsReply)
```

Frees a reply.

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("https://127.0.0.1:1/");
let roots = balloc(0);
match https_fetch(host, name, roots, 3) {
  Option::Some(r) => { https_reply_free(r); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(roots);
bfree(name);
```

### `https_fetch`

```bastio
fn https_fetch(h: &Host, url: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, redirects: u64) -> Option[HttpsReply]
  requires blen(url) < 65536 && blen(roots) < 274877906944 && redirects <= 16
```

Fetches the `https://` URL `url`: looks the host up (its IPv4 address, or
if it has none or the connection fails, its IPv6 address), connects, checks the
server against `roots` and returns the status and body of the answer
(HTTP/1.1 with the connection closed after it; the body is the data behind
the head, with a chunked body decoded). A redirect (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) to a path on the
same server or to another `https://` URL is followed, at most `redirects`
times; a redirect to anything else (plain `http://`, another scheme) is
not followed and its answer is returned as it is. `None` if the URL is
not an acceptable `https://` URL, the name does not resolve, the exchange
fails or the answer has no head.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1 of the loopback.
let url = bfrom("https://127.0.0.1:1/");
let roots = balloc(0);
let mut bad = 0;
match https_fetch(host, url, roots, 3) {
  Option::Some(r) => { https_reply_free(r); bad = 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(roots);
bfree(url);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `https_flush`

```bastio
fn https_flush(h: &Host, sock: u64, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
```

Internal: sends what is in `out` over the socket and empties it. False if sending fails.

### `https_on`

```bastio
fn https_on(h: &Host, sock: u64, name: &Bytes, request: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, rnd: &Bytes) -> HttpsResult
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(request) < 1073741824 && blen(roots) < 274877906944 && blen(rnd) == 96
```

Internal: the exchange over the connected socket `sock`, with the 96
random bytes `rnd`; closes the socket.

### `https_connected`

```bastio
fn https_connected(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64, name: &Bytes, request: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes, rnd: &Bytes) -> Option[HttpsResult]
  requires blen(name) <= 255 && blen(request) < 1073741824 && blen(roots) < 274877906944 && blen(rnd) == 96
```

Internal: `https_exchange` with the 96 random bytes `rnd` already drawn.

### `https_is_redirect`

```bastio
fn https_is_redirect(st: u64) -> bool
```

Internal: is `st` a redirect status that carries a `Location`?

### `https_unchunk`

```bastio
fn https_unchunk(raw: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Option[HttpsChunks]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.end <= blen(raw) && blen(result.Some.body) <= blen(raw)
```

Internal: the chunked body that starts at `at` in `raw`, decoded, or
`None` if it is malformed or not all there (the last chunk and the empty
line after its trailers are missing).

### `https_keep`

```bastio
fn https_keep(raw: &Bytes, state: u64) -> u64
  ensures result <= blen(raw)
```

Internal: how many bytes of the data `raw` (with the final `state` of the
exchange) make up a complete answer, or 0 if it is not: with a
`Content-Length`, the head and that many bytes of body (a cut-off
connection, state 5, is fine then); with a chunked body, up to the end of
its last chunk and trailers (also fine when cut off); without either, all
the data, but only if the server ended it with a close_notify (state 6).
Framing that `http_body` finds ambiguous (both headers, a repeated one,
another transfer coding) is refused.

### `https_complete`

```bastio
fn https_complete(r: HttpsResult) -> Option[Bytes]
```

Internal: the complete answer in `r` (see `https_keep`); a chunked body is
replaced by its decoded data. Frees `r`.

### `https_has`

```bastio
fn https_has(m: &Bytes, name: Str) -> bool
```

Internal: does the head of `m` have the header `name`?

### `https_try4`

```bastio
fn https_try4(h: &Host, u: &HttpsUrl, request: &Bytes, roots: &Bytes) -> Option[HttpsResult]
  requires blen(u.host) <= 255 && blen(request) < 1073741824 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

Internal: `https_exchange` to the IPv4 address of the host of `u`; `None`
if it has none or the connection cannot be made.

### `https_step`

```bastio
fn https_step(h: &Host, u: &HttpsUrl, roots: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(u.host) <= 255 && blen(u.path) < 65536 && blen(roots) < 274877906944
```

Internal: one `GET` of the URL `u`: the whole answer (see `https_complete`).

### `https_redirect`

```bastio
fn https_redirect(raw: &Bytes, u: &HttpsUrl) -> Option[HttpsUrl]
  requires blen(u.host) >= 1 && blen(u.host) <= 255 && u.port >= 1 && u.port <= 65535
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some.host) >= 1 && blen(result.Some.host) <= 255
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.port >= 1 && result.Some.port <= 65535
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some.path) >= 1 && blen(result.Some.path) < 65536
```

Internal: the URL a redirecting `raw` answer from `u` leads to, if it
names one the client may follow (see `httpsurl_follow`).
